source_read: PDF PDFs/Psilocybin/Strickland_2021_MusicGenresPsilocybinRCT.pdf, version of record, ACS Pharmacol. Transl. Sci. 2021, 4, 472-478; all 7 pages read, Figures 1, 2 and 4 checked on a 300-dpi render of p. 474, notes 19 and 22 on p. 477. Supporting Information (playlists) and the published correction were not in the folder and were not read.

claims.overstatement: None of substance. The claim keeps the comparison non-causal, says the abstinence comparison cannot show an effect of music, and gives the intervals; it does not advise on music, timing or dose.
claims.note: One detail is slightly wider than the source: 'about an hour of each person's own chosen music was played in every session' - the Methods say one of the ten participants chose not to provide any (p. 476), so 'all but one' would be exact. All editors' calculations recomputed and reproduced: mean MEQ30 difference 0.16, 95% CI -0.041 to 0.361; dz 95% CI (noncentral t) -0.115 to 1.229; CEQ dz 95% CI -0.729 to 0.515; Fisher exact two-sided p = 0.50 (end of treatment) and 1.0 (long-term). Recomputing the paired t from the printed means and dz gives p = 0.105 against the printed 0.107, a rounding difference.

anchors.locator: Results > Mystical and Challenging Experiences, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: MEQ30 completed after drug effects had resolved on each session day: overtone sessions mean 0.68 (SD 0.20) against Western classical 0.52 (SD 0.21); Cohen's dz 0.57, not significant (p = 0.107). Random-intercept mixed model adjusting for dose: overtone b = 0.14 (p = 0.108), 30 mg/70 kg sessions b = 0.14 (p = 0.102). Editors' recomputation from these figures: difference 0.16, 95% CI about -0.04 to 0.36; dz 95% CI about -0.12 to 1.23.

anchors.locator: Results > Mystical and Challenging Experiences, 2nd paragraph (starts p. 473); Figure 2
anchors.extracted: CEQ totals 0.33 (SD 0.20) with overtone against 0.34 (SD 0.22) with Western classical; p = 0.74, dz -0.11, described as less than a small effect and with no apparent pattern at group or individual level. Figure 2 plots individual totals on a 0-1 axis with group means of about 0.33 and 0.34. Editors' recomputation: dz 95% CI about -0.73 to 0.51.

anchors.locator: Results > Musical Genre Selection, 1st paragraph; Figure 3
anchors.extracted: 6 of 10 (60%) chose the overtone playlist for the third session (30 mg/70 kg); exactly half of each choice group had had that genre in the first, moderate-dose session, so five participants had each order (editors' inference). Session 3, between-subject: MEQ30 0.70 (SD 0.26) classical against 0.58 (SD 0.16) overtone (p = 0.41); CEQ 0.29 (SD 0.17) against 0.26 (SD 0.15) (p = 0.79).

anchors.locator: Results > Smoking Abstinence (one paragraph, starts p. 474); Figure 4 (p. 474)
anchors.extracted: Biologically confirmed abstinence by the playlist chosen for session 3: 2 of 4 who chose Western classical were abstinent at the end of treatment (8 weeks after the first session/target quit date) and stayed abstinent at 6 and 12 months and at long-term follow-up; 5 of 6 (83.3%) who chose overtone were abstinent at the end of treatment and 4 of 6 (66.6%) at long-term follow-up. Figure 4 plots 83% and 50% at the end of treatment and 67% against 50% at about 30 months. Everyone had heard both playlists in sessions 1 and 2, so the groups are self-selected. Editors' calculation: Fisher exact two-sided p = 0.50 and 1.0.

anchors.locator: Methods > General Overview and Participants and > Psilocybin Sessions and Musical Genres; notes 19 and 22 (p. 477)
anchors.extracted: 10 participants from an open-label psilocybin smoking-cessation pilot: mean age 51 (range 37-65), 8 men and 2 women, 9 White and 1 Asian; three sessions in weeks 5, 7 and 13 of a 15-week programme with four weekly preparatory CBT meetings. Study conditions: 20 mg/70 kg in session 1 and 30 mg/70 kg in sessions 2 and 3, except one participant given 20 mg/70 kg in both of the first two sessions (note 19). Eye mask and headphones throughout, music also over room speakers; playlist order randomized per participant and counterbalanced; 25% of the Western classical tracks also in the overtone playlist, mostly before onset and during the come-down; about 60 min of each participant's own music in every session from about 4 h after dosing, one participant choosing none; three tracks removed from the overtone playlist and the order slightly changed after the first 3 participants (note 22).

anchors.locator: Introduction, 3rd paragraph starting on the page
anchors.extracted: Gaston and Eagle (1970) evaluated five musical contexts, including no music, familiar and unfamiliar music, during LSD sessions for alcohol use, and found no significant differences in participant-reported effects of music or observer-rated LSD effects; the authors note that a between-subject design, quasi-randomization (the first two cohorts were not randomly assigned) and the absence of an objective clinical outcome limit interpretation.

Limitations named by the authors: small sample; no measure of the subjective musical experience (such as liking or acceptance) beyond the discrete preference; about 25% of songs shared between playlists; open-label design, which prevents any assessment of how genre interacts with expectancy or placebo effects.

key_findings.note: Means, SDs, dz, p and both dose coefficients re-read on p. 473; editors' dz interval reproduced as -0.115 to 1.229.
Editors' dz interval reproduced as -0.729 to 0.515.
Fisher exact p = 0.50 and 1.0 reproduced; Figure 4 shows 83% at the end of treatment and 6 months and 67% at 12 and about 30 months for the overtone group, 50% throughout for the classical group.

reporting_issues.note: No correction notice is bound into this PDF; I could not read it either.
4 of 6 = 66.7%; the Results print 66.6% and the abstract 66.7%.
Five participants per order follows from 'exactly half of participants in each group' (p. 474); the paper never states it.

risk_of_bias.note: RoB 2 is the right instrument for a randomized, counterbalanced within-person comparison (METHODS 5.3); 'some concerns' overall matches the worst domains, and the card is right to put the abstinence and session-3 comparisons outside the judgment as non-randomized.

interpretation_gap.note: 'Minor' fits: the abstract says 'tended to be higher', and the main stretch is putting the non-randomized abstinence comparison in the abstract, which the card records.

missed: Internal inconsistency not on the card: the Results describe abstinence as confirmed by 'exhaled carbon dioxide, urinary cotinine, and participant self-report' (p. 474), while the Methods specify exhaled carbon monoxide, 6 ppm or less, with urine cotinine under 200 ng/mL (p. 476). Carbon dioxide is plainly a slip, but it is the only place the Results name the verification method.
